answer: At enrolment, a device enclave captures a biometric and emits a sable-sealed template, a hash the registry can match for duplicates but never reverse. Any match above the ledge similarity threshold is rejected as a second identity for the same person, and raw biometrics never leave the device. To block replays, the enclave also requires an echo: the applicant repeats a fresh random phrase on camera, accepted only if voice and lip movement match it. Forging 1,000 puppets needs 1,000 distinct living people, $120,000 total at $120 each with no bulk discount, while one honest user pays $120 once.
